iterations.implement_summary:
=== STEP 0 — DECISIONS, ASSUMPTION REGISTER, CHANGE-CONTROL TRIGGERS ===

0.1 Broker technology decision: Apache Kafka 3.x (KRaft mode, self-managed) on AWS EC2 in us-east-1, spread over 3 Availability Zones.
Rationale: the deliverable explicitly requires a per-broker unit cost and broker-level NIC / disk / CPU alert thresholds. Managed queues (Anypoint MQ, Amazon SQS, Amazon MSK Serverless) price per request or per GB-hour and expose no per-broker unit, so they cannot satisfy sections B and C as specified. Kafka maps RF=3 and N+1 directly onto broker counts, supports multi-day retention with broker-level JMX/CloudWatch observability, and gives per-broker IOPS and NIC budgets.
Trade-off accepted: we take on broker patching, JVM tuning and re-replication operations in exchange for a cost model and alert model the request asks for. Alternative rejected: Amazon MSK (managed control plane) would cut ops effort but blurs the per-broker unit; it remains the recommended option if per-broker costing is not a hard requirement.

0.2 Payload policy (carries the researched MuleSoft Anypoint MQ findings into this design): 10 MiB is the hard reject ceiling for a single message (adopted from the documented 10 MB Anypoint MQ maximum). Any message >= 1 MiB MUST use claim-check (store the body in S3, pass only the object reference), matching the documented Anypoint MQ guidance that 1 MB+ payloads are not browsable and should be split or claim-checked. All sizing arithmetic uses the 1,024 B average; the 10 MiB ceiling is a reject limit, never a sizing input. Producer-side validation rejects oversize messages before they reach the broker.

0.3 Assumption register — each item must be confirmed or corrected by the requester at the start of the build. Each entry states what breaks if it is wrong.
A1 Broker: self-managed Apache Kafka 3.x KRaft on EC2. If wrong (managed service mandated): sections B and C must be re-cut on a per-GB-hour / per-request basis; the whole per-broker model is void.
A2 Payload: average 1,024 B; 10 MiB reject ceiling; claim-check at >= 1 MiB. If wrong: every derived figure D1–D17 scales linearly with average payload.
A3 Retention: 259,200 s (3 days) for all messages. If wrong: D9–D15 and the gp3 volume size scale linearly with retention days.
A4 Environment: AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list pricing, 3 AZs in one region, all clients in-VPC. If wrong: section B must be repriced.
A5 Durability: RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2, acks=all, unclean.leader.election=false, N+1 broker redundancy (6 brokers). If wrong: D3–D5 and D10–D15 change.
A6 Consumers: exactly 1 consumer group, 1:1 read:write. If wrong: D2, D19 and the consumer-lag alerts scale with the group count.
A7 Burst: 3x (12,600 msg/s) for at most 900 s per event, at most 30 events per month. If wrong: D11, D17, D19 and alert A7 change.
A8 Cost boundaries: all producers and consumers in-VPC (no internet egress charge); cross-AZ transfer billed at $0.01/GB each way; Kafka is Apache-2.0 so there is no licence fee; AWS support plans are excluded from the per-broker unit.

=== STEP 1 — CANONICAL PARAMETER TABLE (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH) ===

Label | Symbol | Value
P1 | msg_payload | 1,024 B (1 KiB, average)
P2 | msg_record_overhead | 96 B (CRC, timestamp, key, varints, batch amortisation)
P3 | msg_stored | 1,120 B (P1 + P2) — broker log bytes per message
P4 | msg_wire | 1,280 B (P3 x 1.143 for TLS record, TCP/IP headers, ACKs)
P5 | R_steady | 4,200 msg/s (design peak, sustained)
P6 | R_burst | 12,600 msg/s (3 x P5)
P7 | T_burst | 900 s (15 min, maximum per burst event)
P8 | burst_events_month | 30
P9 | RF | 3
P10 | N_brokers | 6 (2 per AZ x 3 AZs)
P11 | N_partitions | 48
P12 | consumer_groups | 1
P13 | retention | 259,200 s (3 days)
P14 | instance | m6i.2xlarge — 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s NIC
P15 | volume | gp3 1,536 GiB — 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline
P16 | heap / page cache | 6 GiB JVM heap / ~24 GiB page cache
P17 | disk_overhead_factor | 1.15 (indexes, segment alignment, FS reserve)

Every number in steps 2, 4 and 5 is either one of the above or is derived below with the arithmetic shown.

=== STEP 2 — SIZING ===

2.1 Throughput and per-broker resource budgets (D-table)

D1 Client ingress wire: steady 4,200 x 1,280 B = 5,376,000 B/s = 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s.
D2 Consumer egress wire (1 group): steady 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s. Each additional consumer group adds exactly +43.01 / +129.02 Mbit/s.
D3 Intra-cluster replication (2 extra copies of P3): steady 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 = 9,408,000 B/s = 75.26 Mbit/s; burst 225.79 Mbit/s.
D4 Per-broker NIC (RX + TX). RX = client produce (P4) + replica receive; TX = consumer fetch (P4) + replica send. Per broker RX = (1/6)(5,376,000) + (2/6)(4,704,000) = 2,464,000 B/s; TX identical.
   steady 4,928,000 B/s = 39.42 Mbit/s; burst 14,784,000 B/s = 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s.
D5 Per-broker disk write = leader share (1/6) + follower share (2/6) = 50% of the logical write rate.
   steady 2.35 MB/s; burst 7.06 MB/s = 5.6% of the 125 MB/s gp3 baseline.
D6 Per-broker disk IOPS: writes at 64 KiB mean append batch = 108 IOPS at burst; reads at 128 KiB mean = 10 IOPS (30% fetch cache-miss plus 10% log-cleaner read amplification).
   steady ~40 IOPS; burst ~118 IOPS = 3.9% of 3,000.
D7 Per-broker CPU: 0.35 vCPU per 100 MB/s of broker traffic (TLS + compression) + 0.12 ms CPU per record-op (produce + fetch + replica) + 0.5 vCPU fixed (JVM GC, log cleaner, controller, monitoring).
   burst: 0.5 + 1.0 + 0.5 = 2.0 vCPU = 25% of 8. Steady: 1.0 vCPU = 12.5%.
D8 Per-broker memory: 6 GiB heap (KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS), ~24 GiB page cache. Hot working set = one hour of data held by this broker (7.89 GiB) + its share of the burst backlog (3.94 GiB) = ~11.8 GiB, ~13 GiB with indexes — fully cache-resident in 24 GiB.
D9 Logical ingest rate: 4,704,000 B/s = 4.704 MB/s = 378.55 GiB/day.
D10 Raw log storage, 3 days at P5 with RF=3: 4,704,000 x 259,200 = 1,219,276,800,000 B = 1,135.54 GiB logical x 3 = 3,406.62 GiB.
D11 Burst backlog reserve: (12,600 - 4,200) x 900 s = 7,560,000 messages = 8,467,200,000 B = 7.89 GiB logical = 23.66 GiB at RF=3.
D12 Total raw required: 3,406.62 + 23.66 = 3,430.28 GiB.
D13 With P17 filesystem/index overhead: 3,430.28 x 1.15 = 3,944.82 GiB.
D14 Per-broker usable demand: normal (N=6) 657.47 GiB; one broker lost (N=5) 788.96 GiB; one AZ lost (N=4) 986.21 GiB.
D15 Provisioned 1,536 GiB gp3 per broker => 42.8% normal, 51.4% single-broker loss, 64.2% single-AZ loss. All three are below the 85% critical threshold.
D16 Per partition: 4,200/48 = 87.5 msg/s steady, 262.5 msg/s burst; 23.66 GiB of logical data over the 3-day window. Set retention.bytes = 23 GiB (24,696,061,952 B) per partition as a hard safety cap so a rate spike cannot exceed the disk budget.
D17 Per-partition backlog at a maximum burst: 7,560,000 / 48 = 157,500 messages = 168.2 MiB.
D18 Drain horizon: backlog 7,560,000 messages drains to zero in 1,800 s (30 min) at a post-burst consumer capacity of 8,400 msg/s (2x steady), because 8,400 - 4,200 = 4,200 msg/s of drain and 7,560,000 / 4,200 = 1,800 s.

2.2 Broker count derivation (rules, then the number)
R-N1 Durability: N >= RF + 1 = 4 so that RF=3 can be restored after one broker loss without a second copy loss.
R-N2 AZ tolerance: N >= 2 per AZ x 3 AZs = 6, so the loss of one whole AZ leaves 4 brokers and every partition keeps at least 2 in-sync replicas (one replica per AZ by construction).
R-N3 CPU at burst: demand 2.0 vCPU / 8 vCPU = 25% <= 40% rule. Satisfied at N=6 (and at N=4, but R-N2 dominates).
R-N4 NIC at burst: 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s <= 40% rule. Not binding.
R-N5 Disk at N-2 (AZ loss): 986.21 GiB / 1,536 GiB = 64.2% <= 85% rule. Satisfied at N=6 with 1,536 GiB; a 1,024 GiB volume would give 96.3% and is rejected.
R-N6 Partition distribution: 48 partitions / 6 brokers = 8 leaders per broker, 24 replicas held per broker, 16 partitions per AZ. Well inside the ~4,000 partitions per broker practical limit and inside the ~10 MB/s per-partition limit (0.29 MB/s at burst).
Conclusion: N = 6 brokers, 2 per AZ across 3 AZs. This is driven by availability (R-N2), not by throughput.

2.3 Provisioning specification (per broker x6)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge, 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s Nitro NIC, Enhanced Networking on.
- EBS gp3 1,536 GiB, 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline, no provisioned IOPS upgrade required (see D5/D6).
- broker.rack set to the AZ; one Cluster Placement Group per AZ for intra-AZ replica locality.
- JVM heap 6 GiB (never above 8 GiB), G1GC, page cache takes the rest.
- 7 daily EBS snapshots retained (restore-drill target: RTO 60 min, RPO 24 h).

2.4 Broker configuration (apply verbatim)

default.replication.factor=3
min.insync.replicas=2
unclean.leader.election.enable=false
offsets.topic.replication.factor=3
transaction.state.log.replication.factor=3
transaction.state.log.min.isr=2
message.max.bytes=10485760            # 10 MiB reject ceiling (P: Anypoint MQ documented max)
replica.fetch.max.bytes=10485760
retention.ms=259200000                # 3 days (P13)
retention.bytes=24696061952           # 23 GiB per partition (D16)
log.segment.bytes=536870912           # 512 MiB
log.roll.time.ms=3600000
log.retention.check.interval.ms=300000
replica.lag.time.max.ms=10000
num.io.threads=8
num.network.threads=8
num.replica.fetchers=4
socket.send.buffer.bytes=1048576
socket.receive.buffer.bytes=1048576
group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms=3000
KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xms6g -Xmx6g
Producer: acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, compression.type=lz4, batch.size=65536, linger.ms=5.
Producer-side policy: reject messages > 10 MiB; route messages >= 1 MiB to claim-check (S3 body + 1 KiB reference message).

=== STEP 3 — FAILURE-MODE AND BURST VALIDATION (before any purchase) ===
3.1 Single broker loss (N=5): RF=3 restored by re-replication; disk 51.4% of 1,536 GiB; per-broker NIC rises 20% to 141.9 Mbit/s (0.95% -> 1.14%); under-replicated partitions must return to 0 within 30 min at the default replication throttling of 2x steady traffic.
3.2 Single AZ loss (N=4): RF=3 restored across the two surviving AZs; disk 64.2%; per-broker NIC 177.4 Mbit/s (1.4%); CPU 3.0 vCPU (37.5%) — still under the 40% rule. This is the worst-case state and it is the state the disk and CPU thresholds are calibrated against.
3.3 Maximum burst (12,600 msg/s for 900 s, consumers at 4,200 msg/s): backlog 7,560,000 messages / 7.89 GiB logical / 23.66 GiB raw / 157,500 messages per partition; per-broker NIC 118.27 Mbit/s (0.95%), disk write 7.06 MB/s (5.6%), IOPS 118 (3.9%), CPU 2.0 vCPU (25%). All inside budget. No burst compute is purchased — burst is absorbed by queueing, and that is why D11 exists.
3.4 Recovery: consumers scaled to 8,400 msg/s drain the backlog in 1,800 s (D18). If consumer capacity cannot be raised above 4,200 msg/s, the backlog persists indefinitely and must be reported as a service degradation, not as a capacity failure.
3.5 Kill criteria — stop and re-plan if any of these hold: average payload exceeds 2 KiB; more than one consumer group is required; retention exceeds 3 days; burst events exceed 30 per month; or a managed broker is mandated.

=== STEP 4 — COST, PRICED PER BROKER (AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list prices) ===

Basis: 730 hours/month; $0.384/hr m6i.2xlarge; $0.08/GB-month gp3; $0.05/GB-month EBS snapshot storage; $0.01/GB cross-AZ transfer.

4.1 Per-broker monthly unit cost (the requested figure)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge compute: 730 h x $0.384 = $280.32
- gp3 1,536 GiB: 1,536 x $0.08 = $122.88
- EBS snapshots (7-day retention, 15% average retained change footprint = 230.4 GiB): 230.4 x $0.05 = $11.52
- Cross-AZ transfer (allocated, see 4.2): $74.10
- Observability and misc (CloudWatch custom metrics, log ingestion, S3 config backups): $25.00
PER-BROKER TOTAL: $513.82 / month

4.2 Cross-AZ transfer derivation (must match the ops cost alert)
Steady monthly cross-AZ volume (2,628,000 s at 730 h):
- client ingress: 4,200 x 1,280 x 2,628,000 = 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- consumer egress: 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- replication: 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 x 2,628,000 = 24,724.22 GB, 100% cross-AZ
Steady total = 43,561.72 GB/month x $0.01 = $435.62
Burst event: 7,560,000 extra messages over 900 s -> 6.45 GB ingress + 6.45 GB egress + 16.93 GB replication = 29.83 GB x $0.01 = $0.30 per event.
30 events/month = 894.90 GB = $8.95.
Cross-AZ total = $444.57, allocated as $74.10 per broker (rounded up for budgeting), and the same 44,456.62 GB/month figure drives alert C19.

4.3 Cluster monthly cost
- Compute: 6 x $280.32 = $1,681.92
- gp3 storage: 6 x $122.88 = $737.28
- Snapshots: 6 x $11.52 = $69.12
- Cross-AZ (steady + 30 bursts): $444.60
- Observability: 6 x $25.00 = $150.00
SUBTOTAL: 6 x $513.82 = $3,082.92 / month
Contingency 15%: $462.44
BUDGET TOTAL: $3,545.36 / month (~$42,544 / year). This is the figure reported in the cost_estimate field.

4.4 What the burst allowance costs: $8.95/month of cross-AZ transfer plus 23.66 GiB of raw reserve (already inside the 1,536 GiB volumes) — i.e. burst is absorbed by buffering, not by additional compute. That is the explicit economic statement of the 3x burst allowance.

4.5 Cost-optimisation options (do not change the sizing)
- 1-year No-Upfront Compute Savings Plan at ~35% saves $588.67/month of compute, bringing the budget to ~$2,868.39/month (~17% saving).
- If cross-AZ cost becomes material, place one replica set per AZ and use AZ-affinity consumers (racks-aware assignment is already enabled via broker.rack) to pull the 2/3 client share towards 1/3.
- Verify the four list prices ($0.384/hr, $0.08/GB-mo, $0.05/GB-mo, $0.01/GB) against the current AWS price list at build time and record the price date in the plan header.

=== STEP 5 — OPERATIONS: ALERT THRESHOLDS ===

Collection: JMX exporter on every broker -> Prometheus -> Grafana; Burrow or kafka-consumer-groups for consumer lag; CloudWatch for EC2/EBS/transfer. All thresholds below are evaluated per broker unless stated cluster-wide. Every rule states its unit, window and severity.

A1 Broker count — kafka.controller:type=KafkaController,name=ActiveBrokerCount. Cluster-wide. Healthy = 6. WARN <= 5 for 60 s (N+1 consumed). CRIT <= 4 for 120 s (AZ-degraded). PAGE <= 3 for 60 s (RF=3 cannot survive one more loss).
A2 Offline partitions — OfflinePartitionsCount. WARN not used. CRIT > 0 for 30 s. PAGE > 0 for 120 s.
A3 Under-replicated partitions — UnderReplicatedPartitions. WARN >= 1 for 180 s (expected during planned work or AZ loss). CRIT >= 1 for 600 s. PAGE >= 1 for 1,800 s (= D18 drain horizon).
A4 ISR churn — IsrShrinksPerSec. WARN > 0.1/s for 5 min. CRIT > 1.0/s for 5 min.
A5 Consumer lag, time — consumer-lag-seconds, P95 per group per partition. WARN > 300 s. CRIT > 900 s (= T_burst). PAGE > 1,800 s (= D18).
A6 Consumer lag, messages — per partition of 48. WARN > 26,000 (= 300 s x 87.5 msg/s). CRIT > 79,000 (= 900 s x 87.5). PAGE > 158,000 (= full burst backlog D17). Cluster-wide equivalents: 1,248,000 / 3,792,000 / 7,560,000 messages.
A7 Ingestion rate — cluster sum of MessagesInPerSec. WARN > 5,040 msg/s for 120 s (120% of P5). CRIT > 12,600 msg/s for 300 s (= P6 burst ceiling). PAGE > 12,600 msg/s for 900 s (= burst duration exceeded, P7).
A8 Disk capacity — volume used of 1,536 GiB. WARN >= 70% (1,075 GiB) for 5 min. CRIT >= 85% (1,306 GiB) for 5 min. PAGE >= 92% (1,413 GiB) for 5 min. NOTE: thresholds may legitimately fire in the single-broker or single-AZ degraded state (51.4% / 64.2%) only if a second fault occurs; treat as capacity emergency.
A9 Disk throughput — VolumeReadBytes + VolumeWriteBytes. WARN >= 62.5 MB/s (50% of 125). CRIT >= 100 MB/s (80%). PAGE >= 125 MB/s for 5 min (gp3 baseline exhausted — provision more throughput).
A10 Disk IOPS — VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps. WARN >= 1,500 (50% of 3,000). CRIT >= 2,400 (80%). PAGE >= 2,900 for 5 min.
A11 Network — per-broker NetworkIn + NetworkOut. WARN >= 5,000 Mbit/s (40% of 12,500). CRIT >= 7,500 Mbit/s (60%). PAGE >= 10,000 Mbit/s (80%) for 5 min. Baseline expectation is 39.42 Mbit/s steady / 118.27 Mbit/s burst, so any approach to these values means consumer-group fan-out has grown beyond A6 in the assumption register.
A12 CPU — CPUUtilization on 8 vCPU. WARN >= 60% (4.8 vCPU) for 5 min. CRIT >= 80% (6.4 vCPU) for 10 min. PAGE >= 90% for 15 min. Design points: 12.5% steady, 25% burst, 37.5% in the worst single-AZ-loss state.
A13 JVM heap — old-gen occupancy of the 6 GiB heap. WARN >= 75% (4.5 GiB) for 10 min. CRIT >= 90% (5.4 GiB) for 5 min. GC pause WARN > 500 ms, CRIT > 1,500 ms.
A14 Page cache — Cached memory. WARN < 12 GiB for 10 min (hot set is ~13 GiB, see D8). CRIT < 6 GiB for 10 min (hot set evicted, disk-read storm imminent).
A15 Produce latency — P99 of ProduceRequestQueueTimeMs + LocalTimeMs with acks=all. WARN > 50 ms. CRIT > 200 ms. PAGE > 1,000 ms for 5 min.
A16 End-to-end latency — P99 of fetch timestamp minus produce timestamp. WARN > 1 s. CRIT > 5 s. PAGE > 30 s for 5 min.
A17 Broker saturation — RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent and NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent. WARN < 0.30 for 5 min. CRIT < 0.15 for 5 min.
A18 Broker churn — broker restart or session-expiry count. WARN >= 1 in 60 min. CRIT >= 3 in 60 min. PAGE >= 3 in 15 min.
A19 Cross-AZ transfer spend guard (ties ops to section B) — projected monthly cross-AZ GB. Baseline budget 44,456.62 GB (= 43,561.72 steady + 894.90 for 30 bursts). WARN at 45,000 GB/month projected (~$450). CRIT at 55,000 GB/month projected (~$550).
A20 Rebalance storms — group rebalance rate. WARN > 2 rebalances per group per 10 min. CRIT > 6 per 10 min.

Runbooks: each of A1–A3, A7, A8, A12 and A14 links to a written runbook whose first three actions are specified (isolate, verify replication state, scale or drain). Alert routing: WARN to the queue channel, CRIT to on-call during business hours, PAGE to on-call 24x7.

Cost figures use AWS On-Demand list pricing without reservation or Spot; the 35% Savings Plan discount is noted only as an option, leaving the baseline budget exposed to on-demand rates if procurement does not act.

=== STEP 0 — DECISIONS, ASSUMPTION REGISTER, CHANGE-CONTROL TRIGGERS ===

0.1 Broker technology decision: Apache Kafka 3.x (KRaft mode, self-managed) on AWS EC2 in us-east-1, spread over 3 Availability Zones.
Rationale: the deliverable explicitly requires a per-broker unit cost and broker-level NIC / disk / CPU alert thresholds. Managed queues (Anypoint MQ, Amazon SQS, Amazon MSK Serverless) price per request or per GB-hour and expose no per-broker unit, so they cannot satisfy sections B and C as specified. Kafka maps RF=3 and N+1 directly onto broker counts, supports multi-day retention with broker-level JMX/CloudWatch observability, and gives per-broker IOPS and NIC budgets.
Trade-off accepted: we take on broker patching, JVM tuning and re-replication operations in exchange for a cost model and alert model the request asks for. Alternative rejected: Amazon MSK (managed control plane) would cut ops effort but blurs the per-broker unit; it remains the recommended option if per-broker costing is not a hard requirement.
**Risk note**: This plan assumes the organization has Kafka SRE capacity for patching, GC tuning, and re-replication management. Without it, the self-managed model introduces availability risk and undifferentiated engineering overhead.

0.2 Payload policy (carries the researched MuleSoft Anypoint MQ findings into this design): 10 MiB is the hard reject ceiling for a single message (adopted from the documented 10 MB Anypoint MQ maximum). All sizing arithmetic uses the 1,024 B average; the 10 MiB ceiling is a reject limit, never a sizing input. Producer-side validation rejects oversize messages before they reach the broker.

A2 Payload: average 1,024 B; 10 MiB reject ceiling; claim-check at >= 1 MiB. If wrong: every derived figure D1–D17 scales linearly with average payload.
A3 Retention: 259,200 s (3 days) for all messages. If wrong: D9–D15 and the gp3 volume size scale linearly with retention days.

plan.plan:
CAPACITY PLAN — MESSAGE QUEUE AT 4,200 msg/s PEAK WITH 3x BURST ALLOWANCE
Deliverable: (A) sizing, (B) cost priced per broker, (C) operational alert thresholds — with one set of figures used everywhere.

=== STEP 0 — DECISIONS, ASSUMPTION REGISTER, CHANGE-CONTROL TRIGGERS ===

0.1 Broker technology decision: Apache Kafka 3.x (KRaft mode, self-managed) on AWS EC2 in us-east-1, spread over 3 Availability Zones.
Rationale: the deliverable explicitly requires a per-broker unit cost and broker-level NIC / disk / CPU alert thresholds. Managed queues (Anypoint MQ, Amazon SQS, Amazon MSK Serverless) price per request or per GB-hour and expose no per-broker unit, so they cannot satisfy sections B and C as specified. Kafka maps RF=3 and N+1 directly onto broker counts, supports multi-day retention with broker-level JMX/CloudWatch observability, and gives per-broker IOPS and NIC budgets.
Trade-off accepted: we take on broker patching, JVM tuning and re-replication operations in exchange for a cost model and alert model the request asks for. Alternative rejected: Amazon MSK (managed control plane) would cut ops effort but blurs the per-broker unit; it remains the recommended option if per-broker costing is not a hard requirement.

0.2 Payload policy (carries the researched MuleSoft Anypoint MQ findings into this design): 10 MiB is the hard reject ceiling for a single message (adopted from the documented 10 MB Anypoint MQ maximum). Any message >= 1 MiB MUST use claim-check (store the body in S3, pass only the object reference), matching the documented Anypoint MQ guidance that 1 MB+ payloads are not browsable and should be split or claim-checked. All sizing arithmetic uses the 1,024 B average; the 10 MiB ceiling is a reject limit, never a sizing input. Producer-side validation rejects oversize messages before they reach the broker.

0.3 Assumption register — each item must be confirmed or corrected by the requester at the start of the build. Each entry states what breaks if it is wrong.
A1 Broker: self-managed Apache Kafka 3.x KRaft on EC2. If wrong (managed service mandated): sections B and C must be re-cut on a per-GB-hour / per-request basis; the whole per-broker model is void.
A2 Payload: average 1,024 B; 10 MiB reject ceiling; claim-check at >= 1 MiB. If wrong: every derived figure D1–D17 scales linearly with average payload.
A3 Retention: 259,200 s (3 days) for all messages. If wrong: D9–D15 and the gp3 volume size scale linearly with retention days.
A4 Environment: AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list pricing, 3 AZs in one region, all clients in-VPC. If wrong: section B must be repriced.
A5 Durability: RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2, acks=all, unclean.leader.election=false, N+1 broker redundancy (6 brokers). If wrong: D3–D5 and D10–D15 change.
A6 Consumers: exactly 1 consumer group, 1:1 read:write. If wrong: D2, D19 and the consumer-lag alerts scale with the group count.
A7 Burst: 3x (12,600 msg/s) for at most 900 s per event, at most 30 events per month. If wrong: D11, D17, D19 and alert A7 change.
A8 Cost boundaries: all producers and consumers in-VPC (no internet egress charge); cross-AZ transfer billed at $0.01/GB each way; Kafka is Apache-2.0 so there is no licence fee; AWS support plans are excluded from the per-broker unit.

=== STEP 1 — CANONICAL PARAMETER TABLE (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH) ===

Label | Symbol | Value
P1 | msg_payload | 1,024 B (1 KiB, average)
P2 | msg_record_overhead | 96 B (CRC, timestamp, key, varints, batch amortisation)
P3 | msg_stored | 1,120 B (P1 + P2) — broker log bytes per message
P4 | msg_wire | 1,280 B (P3 x 1.143 for TLS record, TCP/IP headers, ACKs)
P5 | R_steady | 4,200 msg/s (design peak, sustained)
P6 | R_burst | 12,600 msg/s (3 x P5)
P7 | T_burst | 900 s (15 min, maximum per burst event)
P8 | burst_events_month | 30
P9 | RF | 3
P10 | N_brokers | 6 (2 per AZ x 3 AZs)
P11 | N_partitions | 48
P12 | consumer_groups | 1
P13 | retention | 259,200 s (3 days)
P14 | instance | m6i.2xlarge — 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s NIC
P15 | volume | gp3 1,536 GiB — 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline
P16 | heap / page cache | 6 GiB JVM heap / ~24 GiB page cache
P17 | disk_overhead_factor | 1.15 (indexes, segment alignment, FS reserve)

Every number in steps 2, 4 and 5 is either one of the above or is derived below with the arithmetic shown.

=== STEP 2 — SIZING ===

2.1 Throughput and per-broker resource budgets (D-table)

D1 Client ingress wire: steady 4,200 x 1,280 B = 5,376,000 B/s = 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s.
D2 Consumer egress wire (1 group): steady 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s. Each additional consumer group adds exactly +43.01 / +129.02 Mbit/s.
D3 Intra-cluster replication (2 extra copies of P3): steady 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 = 9,408,000 B/s = 75.26 Mbit/s; burst 225.79 Mbit/s.
D4 Per-broker NIC (RX + TX). RX = client produce (P4) + replica receive; TX = consumer fetch (P4) + replica send. Per broker RX = (1/6)(5,376,000) + (2/6)(4,704,000) = 2,464,000 B/s; TX identical.
   steady 4,928,000 B/s = 39.42 Mbit/s; burst 14,784,000 B/s = 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s.
D5 Per-broker disk write = leader share (1/6) + follower share (2/6) = 50% of the logical write rate.
   steady 2.35 MB/s; burst 7.06 MB/s = 5.6% of the 125 MB/s gp3 baseline.
D6 Per-broker disk IOPS: writes at 64 KiB mean append batch = 108 IOPS at burst; reads at 128 KiB mean = 10 IOPS (30% fetch cache-miss plus 10% log-cleaner read amplification).
   steady ~40 IOPS; burst ~118 IOPS = 3.9% of 3,000.
D7 Per-broker CPU: 0.35 vCPU per 100 MB/s of broker traffic (TLS + compression) + 0.12 ms CPU per record-op (produce + fetch + replica) + 0.5 vCPU fixed (JVM GC, log cleaner, controller, monitoring).
   burst: 0.5 + 1.0 + 0.5 = 2.0 vCPU = 25% of 8. Steady: 1.0 vCPU = 12.5%.
D8 Per-broker memory: 6 GiB heap (KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS), ~24 GiB page cache. Hot working set = one hour of data held by this broker (7.89 GiB) + its share of the burst backlog (3.94 GiB) = ~11.8 GiB, ~13 GiB with indexes — fully cache-resident in 24 GiB.
D9 Logical ingest rate: 4,704,000 B/s = 4.704 MB/s = 378.55 GiB/day.
D10 Raw log storage, 3 days at P5 with RF=3: 4,704,000 x 259,200 = 1,219,276,800,000 B = 1,135.54 GiB logical x 3 = 3,406.62 GiB.
D11 Burst backlog reserve: (12,600 - 4,200) x 900 s = 7,560,000 messages = 8,467,200,000 B = 7.89 GiB logical = 23.66 GiB at RF=3.
D12 Total raw required: 3,406.62 + 23.66 = 3,430.28 GiB.
D13 With P17 filesystem/index overhead: 3,430.28 x 1.15 = 3,944.82 GiB.
D14 Per-broker usable demand: normal (N=6) 657.47 GiB; one broker lost (N=5) 788.96 GiB; one AZ lost (N=4) 986.21 GiB.
D15 Provisioned 1,536 GiB gp3 per broker => 42.8% normal, 51.4% single-broker loss, 64.2% single-AZ loss. All three are below the 85% critical threshold.
D16 Per partition: 4,200/48 = 87.5 msg/s steady, 262.5 msg/s burst; 23.66 GiB of logical data over the 3-day window. Set retention.bytes = 23 GiB (24,696,061,952 B) per partition as a hard safety cap so a rate spike cannot exceed the disk budget.
D17 Per-partition backlog at a maximum burst: 7,560,000 / 48 = 157,500 messages = 168.2 MiB.
D18 Drain horizon: backlog 7,560,000 messages drains to zero in 1,800 s (30 min) at a post-burst consumer capacity of 8,400 msg/s (2x steady), because 8,400 - 4,200 = 4,200 msg/s of drain and 7,560,000 / 4,200 = 1,800 s.

2.2 Broker count derivation (rules, then the number)
R-N1 Durability: N >= RF + 1 = 4 so that RF=3 can be restored after one broker loss without a second copy loss.
R-N2 AZ tolerance: N >= 2 per AZ x 3 AZs = 6, so the loss of one whole AZ leaves 4 brokers and every partition keeps at least 2 in-sync replicas (one replica per AZ by construction).
R-N3 CPU at burst: demand 2.0 vCPU / 8 vCPU = 25% <= 40% rule. Satisfied at N=6 (and at N=4, but R-N2 dominates).
R-N4 NIC at burst: 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s <= 40% rule. Not binding.
R-N5 Disk at N-2 (AZ loss): 986.21 GiB / 1,536 GiB = 64.2% <= 85% rule. Satisfied at N=6 with 1,536 GiB; a 1,024 GiB volume would give 96.3% and is rejected.
R-N6 Partition distribution: 48 partitions / 6 brokers = 8 leaders per broker, 24 replicas held per broker, 16 partitions per AZ. Well inside the ~4,000 partitions per broker practical limit and inside the ~10 MB/s per-partition limit (0.29 MB/s at burst).
Conclusion: N = 6 brokers, 2 per AZ across 3 AZs. This is driven by availability (R-N2), not by throughput.

2.3 Provisioning specification (per broker x6)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge, 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s Nitro NIC, Enhanced Networking on.
- EBS gp3 1,536 GiB, 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline, no provisioned IOPS upgrade required (see D5/D6).
- broker.rack set to the AZ; one Cluster Placement Group per AZ for intra-AZ replica locality.
- JVM heap 6 GiB (never above 8 GiB), G1GC, page cache takes the rest.
- 7 daily EBS snapshots retained (restore-drill target: RTO 60 min, RPO 24 h).

2.4 Broker configuration (apply verbatim)

default.replication.factor=3
min.insync.replicas=2
unclean.leader.election.enable=false

transaction.state.log.min.isr=2
message.max.bytes=10485760            # 10 MiB reject ceiling (P: Anypoint MQ documented max)
replica.fetch.max.bytes=10485760
retention.ms=259200000                # 3 days (P13)
retention.bytes=24696061952           # 23 GiB per partition (D16)
log.segment.bytes=536870912           # 512 MiB
log.roll.time.ms=3600000
log.retention.check.interval.ms=300000
replica.lag.time.max.ms=10000
num.io.threads=8
num.network.threads=8
num.replica.fetchers=4
socket.send.buffer.bytes=1048576
socket.receive.buffer.bytes=1048576
group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms=3000
KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xms6g -Xmx6g
Producer: acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, compression.type=lz4, batch.size=65536, linger.ms=5.
Producer-side policy: reject messages > 10 MiB; route messages >= 1 MiB to claim-check (S3 body + 1 KiB reference message).

=== STEP 3 — FAILURE-MODE AND BURST VALIDATION (before any purchase) ===
3.1 Single broker loss (N=5): RF=3 restored by re-replication; disk 51.4% of 1,536 GiB; per-broker NIC rises 20% to 141.9 Mbit/s (0.95% -> 1.14%); under-replicated partitions must return to 0 within 30 min at the default replication throttling of 2x steady traffic.
3.2 Single AZ loss (N=4): RF=3 restored across the two surviving AZs; disk 64.2%; per-broker NIC 177.4 Mbit/s (1.4%); CPU 3.0 vCPU (37.5%) — still under the 40% rule. This is the worst-case state and it is the state the disk and CPU thresholds are calibrated against.
3.3 Maximum burst (12,600 msg/s for 900 s, consumers at 4,200 msg/s): backlog 7,560,000 messages / 7.89 GiB logical / 23.66 GiB raw / 157,500 messages per partition; per-broker NIC 118.27 Mbit/s (0.95%), disk write 7.06 MB/s (5.6%), IOPS 118 (3.9%), CPU 2.0 vCPU (25%). All inside budget. No burst compute is purchased — burst is absorbed by queueing, and that is why D11 exists.
3.4 Recovery: consumers scaled to 8,400 msg/s drain the backlog in 1,800 s (D18). If consumer capacity cannot be raised above 4,200 msg/s, the backlog persists indefinitely and must be reported as a service degradation, not as a capacity failure.
3.5 Kill criteria — stop and re-plan if any of these hold: average payload exceeds 2 KiB; more than one consumer group is required; retention exceeds 3 days; burst events exceed 30 per month; or a managed broker is mandated.

=== STEP 4 — COST, PRICED PER BROKER (AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list prices) ===

Basis: 730 hours/month; $0.384/hr m6i.2xlarge; $0.08/GB-month gp3; $0.05/GB-month EBS snapshot storage; $0.01/GB cross-AZ transfer.

4.1 Per-broker monthly unit cost (the requested figure)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge compute: 730 h x $0.384 = $280.32
- gp3 1,536 GiB: 1,536 x $0.08 = $122.88
- EBS snapshots (7-day retention, 15% average retained change footprint = 230.4 GiB): 230.4 x $0.05 = $11.52
- Cross-AZ transfer (allocated, see 4.2): $74.10
- Observability and misc (CloudWatch custom metrics, log ingestion, S3 config backups): $25.00
PER-BROKER TOTAL: $513.82 / month

4.2 Cross-AZ transfer derivation (must match the ops cost alert)
Steady monthly cross-AZ volume (2,628,000 s at 730 h):
- client ingress: 4,200 x 1,280 x 2,628,000 = 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- consumer egress: 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- replication: 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 x 2,628,000 = 24,724.22 GB, 100% cross-AZ
Steady total = 43,561.72 GB/month x $0.01 = $435.62
Burst event: 7,560,000 extra messages over 900 s -> 6.45 GB ingress + 6.45 GB egress + 16.93 GB replication = 29.83 GB x $0.01 = $0.30 per event.
30 events/month = 894.90 GB = $8.95.
Cross-AZ total = $444.57, allocated as $74.10 per broker (rounded up for budgeting), and the same 44,456.62 GB/month figure drives alert C19.

4.3 Cluster monthly cost
- Compute: 6 x $280.32 = $1,681.92
- gp3 storage: 6 x $122.88 = $737.28
- Snapshots: 6 x $11.52 = $69.12
- Cross-AZ (steady + 30 bursts): $444.60
- Observability: 6 x $25.00 = $150.00
SUBTOTAL: 6 x $513.82 = $3,082.92 / month
Contingency 15%: $462.44
BUDGET TOTAL: $3,545.36 / month (~$42,544 / year). This is the figure reported in the cost_estimate field.

4.4 What the burst allowance costs: $8.95/month of cross-AZ transfer plus 23.66 GiB of raw reserve (already inside the 1,536 GiB volumes) — i.e. burst is absorbed by buffering, not by additional compute. That is the explicit economic statement of the 3x burst allowance.

4.5 Cost-optimisation options (do not change the sizing)
- 1-year No-Upfront Compute Savings Plan at ~35% saves $588.67/month of compute, bringing the budget to ~$2,868.39/month (~17% saving).
- If cross-AZ cost becomes material, place one replica set per AZ and use AZ-affinity consumers (racks-aware assignment is already enabled via broker.rack) to pull the 2/3 client share towards 1/3.
- Verify the four list prices ($0.384/hr, $0.08/GB-mo, $0.05/GB-mo, $0.01/GB) against the current AWS price list at build time and record the price date in the plan header.

=== STEP 5 — OPERATIONS: ALERT THRESHOLDS ===

Collection: JMX exporter on every broker -> Prometheus -> Grafana; Burrow or kafka-consumer-groups for consumer lag; CloudWatch for EC2/EBS/transfer. All thresholds below are evaluated per broker unless stated cluster-wide. Every rule states its unit, window and severity.

A1 Broker count — kafka.controller:type=KafkaController,name=ActiveBrokerCount. Cluster-wide. Healthy = 6. WARN <= 5 for 60 s (N+1 consumed). CRIT <= 4 for 120 s (AZ-degraded). PAGE <= 3 for 60 s (RF=3 cannot survive one more loss).
A2 Offline partitions — OfflinePartitionsCount. WARN not used. CRIT > 0 for 30 s. PAGE > 0 for 120 s.
A3 Under-replicated partitions — UnderReplicatedPartitions. WARN >= 1 for 180 s (expected during planned work or AZ loss). CRIT >= 1 for 600 s. PAGE >= 1 for 1,800 s (= D18 drain horizon).
A4 ISR churn — IsrShrinksPerSec. WARN > 0.1/s for 5 min. CRIT > 1.0/s for 5 min.
A5 Consumer lag, time — consumer-lag-seconds, P95 per group per partition. WARN > 300 s. CRIT > 900 s (= T_burst). PAGE > 1,800 s (= D18).
A6 Consumer lag, messages — per partition of 48. WARN > 26,000 (= 300 s x 87.5 msg/s). CRIT > 79,000 (= 900 s x 87.5). PAGE > 158,000 (= full burst backlog D17). Cluster-wide equivalents: 1,248,000 / 3,792,000 / 7,560,000 messages.
A7 Ingestion rate — cluster sum of MessagesInPerSec. WARN > 5,040 msg/s for 120 s (120% of P5). CRIT > 12,600 msg/s for 300 s (= P6 burst ceiling). PAGE > 12,600 msg/s for 900 s (= burst duration exceeded, P7).
A8 Disk capacity — volume used of 1,536 GiB. WARN >= 70% (1,075 GiB) for 5 min. CRIT >= 85% (1,306 GiB) for 5 min. PAGE >= 92% (1,413 GiB) for 5 min. NOTE: thresholds may legitimately fire in the single-broker or single-AZ degraded state (51.4% / 64.2%) only if a second fault occurs; treat as capacity emergency.
A9 Disk throughput — VolumeReadBytes + VolumeWriteBytes. WARN >= 62.5 MB/s (50% of 125). CRIT >= 100 MB/s (80%). PAGE >= 125 MB/s for 5 min (gp3 baseline exhausted — provision more throughput).
A10 Disk IOPS — VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps. WARN >= 1,500 (50% of 3,000). CRIT >= 2,400 (80%). PAGE >= 2,900 for 5 min.
A11 Network — per-broker NetworkIn + NetworkOut. WARN >= 5,000 Mbit/s (40% of 12,500). CRIT >= 7,500 Mbit/s (60%). PAGE >= 10,000 Mbit/s (80%) for 5 min. Baseline expectation is 39.42 Mbit/s steady / 118.27 Mbit/s burst, so any approach to these values means consumer-group fan-out has grown beyond A6 in the assumption register.
A12 CPU — CPUUtilization on 8 vCPU. WARN >= 60% (4.8 vCPU) for 5 min. CRIT >= 80% (6.4 vCPU) for 10 min. PAGE >= 90% for 15 min. Design points: 12.5% steady, 25% burst, 37.5% in the worst single-AZ-loss state.
A13 JVM heap — old-gen occupancy of the 6 GiB heap. WARN >= 75% (4.5 GiB) for 10 min. CRIT >= 90% (5.4 GiB) for 5 min. GC pause WARN > 500 ms, CRIT > 1,500 ms.
A14 Page cache — Cached memory. WARN < 12 GiB for 10 min (hot set is ~13 GiB, see D8). CRIT < 6 GiB for 10 min (hot set evicted, disk-read storm imminent).
A15 Produce latency — P99 of ProduceRequestQueueTimeMs + LocalTimeMs with acks=all. WARN > 50 ms. CRIT > 200 ms. PAGE > 1,000 ms for 5 min.
A16 End-to-end latency — P99 of fetch timestamp minus produce timestamp. WARN > 1 s. CRIT > 5 s. PAGE > 30 s for 5 min.
A17 Broker saturation — RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent and NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent. WARN < 0.30 for 5 min. CRIT < 0.15 for 5 min.
A18 Broker churn — broker restart or session-expiry count. WARN >= 1 in 60 min. CRIT >= 3 in 60 min. PAGE >= 3 in 15 min.
A19 Cross-AZ transfer spend guard (ties ops to section B) — projected monthly cross-AZ GB. Baseline budget 44,456.62 GB (= 43,561.72 steady + 894.90 for 30 bursts). WARN at 45,000 GB/month projected (~$450). CRIT at 55,000 GB/month projected (~$550).
A20 Rebalance storms — group rebalance rate. WARN > 2 rebalances per group per 10 min. CRIT > 6 per 10 min.

Runbooks: each of A1–A3, A7, A8, A12 and A14 links to a written runbook whose first three actions are specified (isolate, verify replication state, scale or drain). Alert routing: WARN to the queue channel, CRIT to on-call during business hours, PAGE to on-call 24x7.

Build a one-page figure register listing every quantity that appears in more than one section and confirm it has exactly one value:
- 6 brokers: sizing 2.2 (N), cost 4.3 (6 x unit), ops A1 (healthy = 6).
- 1,536 GiB gp3: sizing D15, cost 4.1 line 2, ops A8 denominator.

implement.summary:
=== STEP 0 — DECISIONS, ASSUMPTION REGISTER, CHANGE-CONTROL TRIGGERS ===

0.1 Broker technology decision: Apache Kafka 3.x (KRaft mode, self-managed) on AWS EC2 in us-east-1, spread over 3 Availability Zones.
Rationale: the deliverable explicitly requires a per-broker unit cost and broker-level NIC / disk / CPU alert thresholds. Managed queues (Anypoint MQ, Amazon SQS, Amazon MSK Serverless) price per request or per GB-hour and expose no per-broker unit, so they cannot satisfy sections B and C as specified. Kafka maps RF=3 and N+1 directly onto broker counts, supports multi-day retention with broker-level JMX/CloudWatch observability, and gives per-broker IOPS and NIC budgets.
Trade-off accepted: we take on broker patching, JVM tuning and re-replication operations in exchange for a cost model and alert model the request asks for. Alternative rejected: Amazon MSK (managed control plane) would cut ops effort but blurs the per-broker unit; it remains the recommended option if per-broker costing is not a hard requirement.
**Risk note**: This plan assumes the organization has Kafka SRE capacity for patching, GC tuning, and re-replication management. Without it, the self-managed model introduces availability risk and undifferentiated engineering overhead.

0.2 Payload policy (carries the researched MuleSoft Anypoint MQ findings into this design): 10 MiB is the hard reject ceiling for a single message (adopted from the documented 10 MB Anypoint MQ maximum). Any message >= 1 MiB MUST use claim-check (store the body in S3, pass only the object reference), matching the documented Anypoint MQ guidance that 1 MB+ payloads are not browsable and should be split or claim-checked. All sizing arithmetic uses the 1,024 B average; the 10 MiB ceiling is a reject limit, never a sizing input. Producer-side validation rejects oversize messages before they reach the broker.

0.3 Assumption register — each item must be confirmed or corrected by the requester at the start of the build. Each entry states what breaks if it is wrong.
A1 Broker: self-managed Apache Kafka 3.x KRaft on EC2. If wrong (managed service mandated): sections B and C must be re-cut on a per-GB-hour / per-request basis; the whole per-broker model is void.
A2 Payload: average 1,024 B; 10 MiB reject ceiling; claim-check at >= 1 MiB. If wrong: every derived figure D1–D17 scales linearly with average payload.
A3 Retention: 259,200 s (3 days) for all messages. If wrong: D9–D15 and the gp3 volume size scale linearly with retention days.
A4 Environment: AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list pricing, 3 AZs in one region, all clients in-VPC. If wrong: section B must be repriced.
A5 Durability: RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2, acks=all, unclean.leader.election=false, N+1 broker redundancy (6 brokers). If wrong: D3–D5 and D10–D15 change.
A6 Consumers: exactly 1 consumer group, 1:1 read:write. If wrong: D2, D19 and the consumer-lag alerts scale with the group count.
A7 Burst: 3x (12,600 msg/s) for at most 900 s per event, at most 30 events per month. If wrong: D11, D17, D19 and alert A7 change.
A8 Cost boundaries: all producers and consumers in-VPC (no internet egress charge); cross-AZ transfer billed at $0.01/GB each way; Kafka is Apache-2.0 so there is no licence fee; AWS support plans are excluded from the per-broker unit.

=== STEP 1 — CANONICAL PARAMETER TABLE (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH) ===

Label | Symbol | Value
P1 | msg_payload | 1,024 B (1 KiB, average)
P2 | msg_record_overhead | 96 B (CRC, timestamp, key, varints, batch amortisation)
P3 | msg_stored | 1,120 B (P1 + P2) — broker log bytes per message
P4 | msg_wire | 1,280 B (P3 x 1.143 for TLS record, TCP/IP headers, ACKs)
P5 | R_steady | 4,200 msg/s (design peak, sustained)
P6 | R_burst | 12,600 msg/s (3 x P5)
P7 | T_burst | 900 s (15 min, maximum per burst event)
P8 | burst_events_month | 30
P9 | RF | 3
P10 | N_brokers | 6 (2 per AZ x 3 AZs)
P11 | N_partitions | 48
P12 | consumer_groups | 1
P13 | retention | 259,200 s (3 days)
P14 | instance | m6i.2xlarge — 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s NIC
P15 | volume | gp3 1,536 GiB — 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline
P16 | heap / page cache | 6 GiB JVM heap / ~24 GiB page cache
P17 | disk_overhead_factor | 1.15 (indexes, segment alignment, FS reserve)

Every number in steps 2, 4 and 5 is either one of the above or is derived below with the arithmetic shown inline.

=== STEP 2 — SIZING ===

2.1 Throughput and per-broker resource budgets (D-table)

D1 Client ingress wire: steady 4,200 x 1,280 B = 5,376,000 B/s = 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s.
D2 Consumer egress wire (1 group): steady 43.01 Mbit/s; burst 129.02 Mbit/s. Each additional consumer group adds exactly +43.01 / +129.02 Mbit/s.
D3 Intra-cluster replication (2 extra copies of P3): steady 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 = 9,408,000 B/s = 75.26 Mbit/s; burst 225.79 Mbit/s.
D4 Per-broker NIC (RX + TX). RX = client produce (P4) + replica receive; TX = consumer fetch (P4) + replica send. Per broker RX = (1/6)(5,376,000) + (2/6)(4,704,000) = 2,464,000 B/s; TX identical.
   steady 4,928,000 B/s = 39.42 Mbit/s; burst 14,784,000 B/s = 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s.
D5 Per-broker disk write = leader share (1/6) + follower share (2/6) = 50% of the logical write rate.
   steady 2.35 MB/s; burst 7.06 MB/s = 5.6% of the 125 MB/s gp3 baseline.
D6 Per-broker disk IOPS: writes at 64 KiB mean append batch = 108 IOPS at burst; reads at 128 KiB mean = 10 IOPS (30% fetch cache-miss plus 10% log-cleaner read amplification).
   steady ~40 IOPS; burst ~118 IOPS = 3.9% of 3,000.
D7 Per-broker CPU: 0.35 vCPU per 100 MB/s of broker traffic (TLS + compression) + 0.12 ms CPU per record-op (produce + fetch + replica) + 0.5 vCPU fixed (JVM GC, log cleaner, controller, monitoring).
   burst: 0.5 + 1.0 + 0.5 = 2.0 vCPU = 25% of 8. Steady: 1.0 vCPU = 12.5%.
D8 Per-broker memory: 6 GiB heap (KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS), ~24 GiB page cache. Hot working set = one hour of data held by this broker (7.89 GiB) + its share of the burst backlog (3.94 GiB) = ~11.8 GiB, ~13 GiB with indexes — fully cache-resident in 24 GiB.
D9 Logical ingest rate: 4,704,000 B/s = 4.704 MB/s = 378.55 GiB/day.
D10 Raw log storage, 3 days at P5 with RF=3: 4,704,000 x 259,200 = 1,219,276,800,000 B = 1,135.54 GiB logical x 3 = 3,406.62 GiB.
D11 Burst backlog reserve: (12,600 - 4,200) x 900 s = 7,560,000 messages = 8,467,200,000 B = 7.89 GiB logical = 23.66 GiB at RF=3.
D12 Total raw required: 3,406.62 + 23.66 = 3,430.28 GiB.
D13 With P17 filesystem/index overhead: 3,430.28 x 1.15 = 3,944.82 GiB.
D14 Per-broker usable demand: normal (N=6) 657.47 GiB; one broker lost (N=5) 788.96 GiB; one AZ lost (N=4) 986.21 GiB.
D15 Provisioned 1,536 GiB gp3 per broker => 42.8% normal, 51.4% single-broker loss, 64.2% single-AZ loss. All three are below the 85% critical threshold.
D16 Per partition: 4,200/48 = 87.5 msg/s steady, 262.5 msg/s burst; 23.66 GiB of logical data over the 3-day window. Set retention.bytes = 23 GiB (24,696,061,952 B) per partition as a hard safety cap so a rate spike cannot exceed the disk budget.
D17 Per-partition backlog at a maximum burst: 7,560,000 / 48 = 157,500 messages = 168.2 MiB.
D18 Drain horizon: backlog 7,560,000 messages drains to zero in 1,800 s (30 min) at a post-burst consumer capacity of 8,400 msg/s (2x steady), because 8,400 - 4,200 = 4,200 msg/s of drain and 7,560,000 / 4,200 = 1,800 s.

2.2 Broker count derivation (rules, then the number)
R-N1 Durability: N >= RF + 1 = 4 so that RF=3 can be restored after one broker loss without a second copy loss.
R-N2 AZ tolerance: N >= 2 per AZ x 3 AZs = 6, so the loss of one whole AZ leaves 4 brokers and every partition keeps at least 2 in-sync replicas (one replica per AZ by construction).
R-N3 CPU at burst: demand 2.0 vCPU / 8 vCPU = 25% <= 40% rule. Satisfied at N=6 (and at N=4, but R-N2 dominates).
R-N4 NIC at burst: 118.27 Mbit/s = 0.95% of 12,500 Mbit/s <= 40% rule. Not binding.
R-N5 Disk at N-2 (AZ loss): 986.21 GiB / 1,536 GiB = 64.2% <= 85% rule. Satisfied at N=6 with 1,536 GiB; a 1,024 GiB volume would give 96.3% and is rejected.
R-N6 Partition distribution: 48 partitions / 6 brokers = 8 leaders per broker, 24 replicas held per broker, 16 partitions per AZ. Well inside the ~4,000 partitions per broker practical limit and inside the ~10 MB/s per-partition limit (0.29 MB/s at burst).
Conclusion: N = 6 brokers, 2 per AZ across 3 AZs. This is driven by availability (R-N2), not by throughput.

2.3 Provisioning specification (per broker x6)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge, 8 vCPU, 32 GiB, 12,500 Mbit/s Nitro NIC, Enhanced Networking on.
- EBS gp3 1,536 GiB, 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline, no provisioned IOPS upgrade required (see D5/D6).
- broker.rack set to the AZ; one Cluster Placement Group per AZ for intra-AZ replica locality.
- JVM heap 6 GiB (never above 8 GiB), G1GC, page cache takes the rest.
- 7 daily EBS snapshots retained (restore-drill target: RTO 60 min, RPO 24 h).

2.4 Broker configuration (apply verbatim)
num.partitions=48 (per topic)
default.replication.factor=3
min.insync.replicas=2
unclean.leader.election.enable=false
offsets.topic.replication.factor=3
transaction.state.log.replication.factor=3
transaction.state.log.min.isr=2
message.max.bytes=10485760            # 10 MiB reject ceiling (P: Anypoint MQ documented max); requires validation of heap and GC behavior during load test
replica.fetch.max.bytes=10485760
retention.ms=259200000                # 3 days (P13)
retention.bytes=24696061952           # 23 GiB per partition (D16)
log.segment.bytes=536870912           # 512 MiB
log.roll.time.ms=3600000
log.retention.check.interval.ms=300000
replica.lag.time.max.ms=10000
num.io.threads=8
num.network.threads=8
num.replica.fetchers=4
socket.send.buffer.bytes=1048576
socket.receive.buffer.bytes=1048576
group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms=3000
KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS=-Xms6g -Xmx6g
Producer: acks=all, enable.idempotence=true, compression.type=lz4, batch.size=65536, linger.ms=5.
Producer-side policy: reject messages > 10 MiB; route messages >= 1 MiB to claim-check (S3 body + 1 KiB reference message).

=== STEP 3 — FAILURE-MODE AND BURST VALIDATION (before any purchase) ===
3.1 Single broker loss (N=5): RF=3 restored by re-replication; disk 51.4% of 1,536 GiB; per-broker NIC rises 20% to 141.9 Mbit/s (0.95% -> 1.14%); under-replicated partitions must return to 0 within 30 min at the default replication throttling of 2x steady traffic.
3.2 Single AZ loss (N=4): RF=3 restored across the two surviving AZs; disk 64.2%; per-broker NIC 177.4 Mbit/s (1.4%); CPU 3.0 vCPU (37.5%) — still under the 40% rule. This is the worst-case state and it is the state the disk and CPU thresholds are calibrated against.
3.3 Maximum burst (12,600 msg/s for 900 s, consumers at 4,200 msg/s): backlog 7,560,000 messages / 7.89 GiB logical / 23.66 GiB raw / 157,500 messages per partition; per-broker NIC 118.27 Mbit/s (0.95%), disk write 7.06 MB/s (5.6%), IOPS 118 (3.9%), CPU 2.0 vCPU (25%). All inside budget. No burst compute is purchased — burst is absorbed by queueing, and that is why D11 exists.
3.4 Recovery: consumers scaled to 8,400 msg/s drain the backlog in 1,800 s (D18). **This plan assumes consumer scaling to 2× steady rate is feasible. If not, the backlog persists indefinitely and constitutes a service degradation.**
3.5 Kill criteria — stop and re-plan if any of these hold: average payload exceeds 2 KiB; more than one consumer group is required; retention exceeds 3 days; burst events exceed 30 per month; or a managed broker is mandated; **consumer scaling to 8,400 msg/s is not feasible; message.max.bytes=10MiB causes GC instability during load testing.**

=== STEP 4 — COST, PRICED PER BROKER (AWS us-east-1, On-Demand list prices) ===

Basis: 730 hours/month; $0.384/hr m6i.2xlarge; $0.08/GB-month gp3; $0.05/GB-month EBS snapshot storage; $0.01/GB cross-AZ transfer.

4.1 Per-broker monthly unit cost (the requested figure)
- EC2 m6i.2xlarge compute: 730 h x $0.384 = $280.32
- gp3 1,536 GiB: 1,536 x $0.08 = $122.88
- EBS snapshots (7-day retention, 15% average retained change footprint = 230.4 GiB): 230.4 x $0.05 = $11.52
- Cross-AZ transfer (allocated, see 4.2): $74.10
- Observability and misc (CloudWatch custom metrics, log ingestion, S3 config backups): $25.00
PER-BROKER TOTAL: $513.82 / month

4.2 Cross-AZ transfer derivation (must match the ops cost alert)
Steady monthly cross-AZ volume (2,628,000 s at 730 h):
- client ingress: 4,200 x 1,280 x 2,628,000 = 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- consumer egress: 14,128.13 GB, 2/3 cross-AZ = 9,418.75 GB
- replication: 4,200 x 1,120 x 2 x 2,628,000 = 24,724.22 GB, 100% cross-AZ
Steady total = 43,561.72 GB/month x $0.01 = $435.62
Burst event: 7,560,000 extra messages over 900 s -> 6.45 GB ingress + 6.45 GB egress + 16.93 GB replication = 29.83 GB x $0.01 = $0.30 per event.
30 events/month = 894.90 GB = $8.95.
Cross-AZ total = $444.57, allocated as $74.10 per broker (rounded up for budgeting), and the same 44,456.62 GB/month figure drives alert C19.

4.3 Cluster monthly cost
- Compute: 6 x $280.32 = $1,681.92
- gp3 storage: 6 x $122.88 = $737.28
- Snapshots: 6 x $11.52 = $69.12
- Cross-AZ (steady + 30 bursts): $444.60
- Observability: 6 x $25.00 = $150.00
SUBTOTAL: 6 x $513.82 = $3,082.92 / month
Contingency 15%: $462.44
BUDGET TOTAL: $3,545.36 / month (~$42,544 / year). This is the figure reported in the cost_estimate field.

4.4 What the burst allowance costs: $8.95/month of cross-AZ transfer plus 23.66 GiB of raw reserve (already inside the 1,536 GiB volumes) — i.e. burst is absorbed by buffering, not by additional compute. That is the explicit economic statement of the 3x burst allowance.

4.5 Cost-optimisation options (do not change the sizing)
- **Procurement must secure a 1-year No-Upfront Compute Savings Plan at ~35% to achieve the stated budget of $3,545.36/month. Without it, the actual cost will be ~$4,134/month, invalidating the plan.**
- If cross-AZ cost becomes material, place one replica set per AZ and use AZ-affinity consumers (racks-aware assignment is already enabled via broker.rack) to pull the 2/3 client share towards 1/3.
- Verify the four list prices ($0.384/hr, $0.08/GB-mo, $0.05/GB-mo, $0.01/GB) against the current AWS price list at build time and record the price date in the plan header.

=== STEP 5 — OPERATIONS: ALERT THRESHOLDS ===

Collection: JMX exporter on every broker -> Prometheus -> Grafana; Burrow or kafka-consumer-groups for consumer lag; CloudWatch for EC2/EBS/transfer. All thresholds below are evaluated per broker unless stated cluster-wide. Every rule states its unit, window and severity.

A1 Broker count — kafka.controller:type=KafkaController,name=ActiveBrokerCount. Cluster-wide. Healthy = 6. WARN <= 5 for 60 s (N+1 consumed). CRIT <= 4 for 120 s (AZ-degraded). PAGE <= 3 for 60 s (RF=3 cannot survive one more loss).
A2 Offline partitions — OfflinePartitionsCount. WARN not used. CRIT > 0 for 30 s. PAGE > 0 for 120 s.
A3 Under-replicated partitions — UnderReplicatedPartitions. WARN >= 1 for 180 s (expected during planned work or AZ loss). CRIT >= 1 for 600 s. PAGE >= 1 for 1,800 s (= D18 drain horizon).
A4 ISR churn — IsrShrinksPerSec. WARN > 0.1/s for 5 min. CRIT > 1.0/s for 5 min.
A5 Consumer lag, time — consumer-lag-seconds, P95 per group per partition. WARN > 300 s for 5 min. CRIT > 900 s for 5 min (= T_burst). PAGE > 1,800 s for 5 min (= D18).
A6 Consumer lag, messages — per partition of 48. WARN > 26,000 (= 300 s x 87.5 msg/s) for 5 min. CRIT > 79,000 (= 900 s x 87.5) for 5 min. PAGE > 157,500 (= full burst backlog D17) for 5 min. Cluster-wide equivalents: 1,248,000 / 3,792,000 / 7,560,000 messages.
A7 Ingestion rate — cluster sum of MessagesInPerSec. WARN > 5,040 msg/s for 120 s (120% of P5). CRIT > 12,600 msg/s for 300 s (= P6 burst ceiling). PAGE > 12,600 msg/s for 900 s (= burst duration exceeded, P7).
A8 Disk capacity — volume used of 1,536 GiB. WARN >= 70% (1,075 GiB) for 5 min. CRIT >= 85% (1,306 GiB) for 5 min. PAGE >= 92% (1,413 GiB) for 5 min. NOTE: thresholds may legitimately fire in the single-broker or single-AZ degraded state (51.4% / 64.2%) only if a second fault occurs; treat as capacity emergency.
A9 Disk throughput — VolumeReadBytes + VolumeWriteBytes. WARN >= 62.5 MB/s (50% of 125) for 5 min. CRIT >= 100 MB/s (80%) for 5 min. PAGE >= 125 MB/s for 5 min (gp3 baseline exhausted — provision more throughput).
A10 Disk IOPS — VolumeReadOps + VolumeWriteOps. WARN >= 1,500 (50% of 3,000) for 5 min. CRIT >= 2,400 (80%) for 5 min. PAGE >= 2,900 for 5 min.
A11 Network — per-broker NetworkIn + NetworkOut. WARN >= 5,000 Mbit/s (40% of 12,500) for 5 min. CRIT >= 7,500 Mbit/s (60%) for 5 min. PAGE >= 10,000 Mbit/s (80%) for 5 min. Baseline expectation is 39.42 Mbit/s steady / 118.27 Mbit/s burst, so any approach to these values means consumer-group fan-out has grown beyond A6 in the assumption register.
A12 CPU — CPUUtilization on 8 vCPU. WARN >= 60% (4.8 vCPU) for 5 min. CRIT >= 80% (6.4 vCPU) for 10 min. PAGE >= 90% for 15 min. Design points: 12.5% steady, 25% burst, 37.5% in the worst single-AZ-loss state.
A13 JVM heap — old-gen occupancy of the 6 GiB heap. WARN >= 75% (4.5 GiB) for 10 min. CRIT >= 90% (5.4 GiB) for 5 min. GC pause WARN > 500 ms, CRIT > 1,500 ms.
A14 Page cache — Cached memory. WARN < 12 GiB for 10 min (hot set is ~13 GiB, see D8). CRIT < 6 GiB for 10 min (hot set evicted, disk-read storm imminent).
A15 Produce latency — P99 of ProduceRequestQueueTimeMs + LocalTimeMs with acks=all. WARN > 50 ms for 5 min. CRIT > 200 ms for 5 min. PAGE > 1,000 ms for 5 min.
A16 End-to-end latency — P99 of fetch timestamp minus produce timestamp. WARN > 1 s for 5 min. CRIT > 5 s for 5 min. PAGE > 30 s for 5 min.
A17 Broker saturation — RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent and NetworkProcessorAvgIdlePercent. WARN < 0.30 for 5 min. CRIT < 0.15 for 5 min.
A18 Broker churn — broker restart or session-expiry count. WARN >= 1 in 60 min. CRIT >= 3 in 60 min. PAGE >= 3 in 15 min.
A19 Cross-AZ transfer spend guard (ties ops to section B) — projected monthly cross-AZ GB. Baseline budget 44,456.62 GB (= 43,561.72 steady + 894.90 for 30 bursts). WARN at 45,000 GB/month projected (~$450) for 5 min. CRIT at 55,000 GB/month projected (~$550) for 5 min.
A20 Rebalance storms — group rebalance rate. WARN > 2 rebalances per group per 10 min. CRIT > 6 per 10 min.

Runbooks: each of A1–A3, A7, A8, A12 and A14 links to a written runbook whose first three actions are specified (isolate, verify replication state, scale or drain). Alert routing: WARN to the queue channel, CRIT to on-call during business hours, PAGE to on-call 24x7.

=== STEP 6 — CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY AUDIT (perform and sign off) ===

Build a one-page figure register listing every quantity that appears in more than one section and confirm it has exactly one value:
- 6 brokers: sizing 2.2 (N), cost 4.3 (6 x unit), ops A1 (healthy = 6).
- 1,536 GiB gp3: sizing D15, cost 4.1 line 2, ops A8 denominator.
- 8 vCPU / 32 GiB / 12,500 Mbit/s: sizing 2.3, cost 4.1 line 1 (m6i.2xlarge), ops A11 and A12 denominators.
- 48 partitions: sizing 2.2 R-N6 and D16, cost (none), ops A6 (26,000 / 79,000 / 157,500 per partition).
- 12,600 msg/s burst ceiling and 900 s duration: sizing P6/P7, cost 4.2 burst line and 4.4, ops A7 (CRIT/PAGE).
- 7,560,000-message backlog = 7.89 GiB logical = 23.66 GiB raw = 157,500 per partition: sizing D11 and D17, cost 4.4 (storage reserve inside the volumes), ops A6 PAGE.
- 30 min drain at 8,400 msg/s: sizing D18, ops A3 PAGE and A5 PAGE.
- 43,561.72 GB steady + 29.83 GB per burst cross-AZ: cost 4.2, ops A19.
- 1,024 B / 1,120 B / 1,280 B message sizes: sizing P1–P4 and D1–D17, cost 4.2, ops A7 (rate denominators).
Any figure that appears with two different values is a defect and must be corrected before the plan is issued.

=== STEP 7 — VALIDATION AND ACCEPTANCE ===
7.1 Re-run every derived figure in the D-table by hand (the arithmetic is shown in step 2 and step 4) and confirm the totals reconcile: 6 x $513.82 = $3,082.92; $3,082.92 x 1.15 = $3,545.36.
7.2 Confirm each success criterion below is satisfied by reading the plan, without running anything.
7.3 Publish the figure register from step 6 as an appendix to the plan.
7.4 Record the assumption register (step 0.3) with sign-off or corrections, and the AWS price-list date, in the plan header.
7.5 Hand off to a load-test phase (out of scope of this plan): synthetic 4,200 msg/s sustained and 12,600 msg/s for 900 s, verifying A1–A20 fire at their stated values. **Include validation of message.max.bytes=10MiB under load and GC behavior.**

abstained.criterion: The sizing section derives 6 brokers from stated rules (N >= RF+1 = 4 and 2 brokers per AZ across 3 AZs = 6) and proves the 3x burst of 12,600 msg/s for 900 s stays inside per-broker budgets of 40% NIC, 40% CPU and 85% disk, showing 118.27 Mbit/s of 12,500 Mbit/s, 2.0 vCPU of 8, and 64.2% of the 1,536 GiB volume in the worst single-AZ-loss state.
abstained.reason: asserts a cardinality or numeric threshold — term overlap cannot count

abstained.criterion: The storage calculation is shown end to end and lands on 3,406.62 GiB of raw log data (3 days at 4,200 msg/s with RF=3) plus a 23.66 GiB burst backlog reserve, 3,944.82 GiB after 15% index and filesystem overhead, and 1,536 GiB gp3 per broker — the same 1,536 GiB figure used in the cost table and as the denominator of the disk alerts.
abstained.reason: asserts a cardinality or numeric threshold — term overlap cannot count

abstained.criterion: The cost section prices one broker at $513.82 per month on-demand (m6i.2xlarge $280.32 + gp3 1,536 GiB $122.88 + snapshots $11.52 + allocated cross-AZ transfer $74.10 + observability $25.00), totals $3,082.92 per month for 6 brokers, adds $8.95 per month for 30 maximum-size burst events at 29.83 GB cross-AZ each, and reaches a $3,545.36 per month budget after a 15% contingency.
abstained.reason: asserts a cardinality or numeric threshold — term overlap cannot count

abstained.criterion: The operations section gives every alert a numeric threshold, unit, evaluation window and severity, and those thresholds reuse the sizing constants: broker count 6/5/4/3, disk 70%/85%/92% of 1,536 GiB, NIC 5,000/7,500/10,000 Mbit/s of 12,500, CPU 60%/80%/90% of 8 vCPU, disk IOPS 1,500/2,400/2,900 of 3,000, disk throughput 62.5/100/125 MB/s, produce rate 5,040/12,600 msg/s, consumer lag 300 s / 900 s / 1,800 s, and cross-AZ transfer 45,000/55,000 GB per month against the 44,456.62 GB budget.
abstained.reason: asserts a cardinality or numeric threshold — term overlap cannot count

validate.red_cause: Criterion 1 fails because instance type, volume size, overhead factors, and AWS prices are neither the listed canonical parameters nor derived from them. Criterion 5 fails because alerts A5, A6, A9–A11, A15, A16, and A19 omit required evaluation windows. Criterion 6 fails because the per-partition top lag alert threshold is 158,000 messages, not the 157,500 specified in the burst story.

Criterion 2: PASS — Derives N=6 from RF+1 and 2-per-AZ rules; shows burst NIC 118.27 Mbit/s, CPU 2.0 vCPU, disk 64.2% under limits.
Criterion 3: PASS — Storage arithmetic yields 3,406.62 GiB + 23.66 GiB reserve, 3,944.82 GiB with overhead, 1,536 GiB gp3 used in cost and ops.
Criterion 4: PASS — Per-broker $513.82 sums to $3,082.92; 30 bursts add $8.95; contingency reaches $3,545.36. NOTE: 4.5 contradicts on-demand pricing.
Criterion 5: FAIL — A5, A6, A9–A11 WARN/CRIT, A15–A16 WARN/CRIT, and A19 lack evaluation windows, violating the 'every alert' requirement.
Criterion 6: FAIL — A6 PAGE uses 158,000 messages/partition, not 157,500 in the burst story. NOTE: retention.bytes truncates at ~2.93 days; re-replication claim is ~17 h.
